senses.def: action of being dedicated to the service of and loyalty to deity
senses.comment: Though in certain contexts ἁγιάζω[a] and ἁγιασμός suggest resulting moral behavior, the emphasis is not upon a manner of life but upon religious activity and observances which reflect one’s dedication or consecration to God. Accordingly, in 1 Corinthians 1:2 one may translate ἁγιάζω as ‘who have given themselves to God’ or ‘who serve God with a whole heart.’

senses.def: to utter words in a melodic pattern
pertaining to being ritually unacceptable, either as the result of defilement or because of the very nature of the object itself (for example, ritually unacceptable animals)
senses.comment: It is possible that there is some subtle distinction in meaning, particularly on a connotative level, between κοινός[b] and ἀκάθαρτος in Acts 10:14, but it is difficult to determine the precise differences of meaning on the basis of existing contexts. The two terms are probably used in Acts 10:14 primarily for the sake of emphasis.

senses.def: to cause a difference by altering the character or nature of something
to exchange one thing for another
the capital of southeast Macedonia
pertaining to a lack of salt
senses.comment: In some languages one may render ‘if the salt has become saltless’ as ‘if the salt no longer tastes like salt,’ but for a discussion of some of the basic problems involved in a rendering of Mark 9:50, see 5.25.

senses.def: pertaining to enduring difficulties without becoming angry or upset
the means or instrument by which release or deliverance is made possible
to await eagerly or expectantly for some future event
to continue to remain in a state until an expected event

senses.subdomain: Enjoy, Take Pleasure In, Be Fond of Doing
senses.def: enjoyment based upon the satisfaction of one’s desires
a marker of result as an inference from what has preceded (frequently used in questions and in the result clause of conditional sentences)
a marker of the possibility of something being true
a degree of uncertainty
one who causes something to begin
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἀρχηγός in Hebrews 2:10, see ἀρχηγός[b] 36.6.

senses.def: a person who as originator or founder of a movement continues as the leader
senses.comment: In order to indicate clearly the significance of ἀρχηγός in Hebrews 2:10, it may be important to employ a translation such as ‘who established a way of salvation and leads people to it.’ But it is also possible to understand ἀρχηγός in Hebrews 2:10 as meaning only the ‘initiator’ or ‘founder’ (see ἀρχηγός[a] 68.2).

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: behavior which shows lack of concern or thought for the consequences of an action
senses.comment: In some languages ἀσωτία in Ephesians 5:18 may be rendered as ‘what one does without being able to think about it’ or ‘what one does when the mind is absent.’

senses.subdomain: Belong To, Be Included in the Membership of, Be Excluded From
senses.def: to exclude or remove someone from an association
senses.comment: It is, of course, possible to translate ἀφορίζω in Luke 6:22 as ‘not to welcome,’ but the emphasis of ἀφορίζω is to exclude from a relationship which has previously existed. One may therefore translate Luke 6:22 as ‘happy are you … when people no longer welcome you in their company … because of the Son of Man.’ By introducing the temporal element ‘no longer,’ the fact of exclusion is made clear.

senses.subdomain: Assign to a Role or Function
senses.def: to set aside a person for a particular task or function
to separate into two or more parts or groups, often by some intervening space
glosses: to set one apart from another

senses.def: a female ruler who has absolute authority within a particular area and who is able to pass on the power to rule to a successor
senses.comment: For an analysis of the use of Κανδάκη in Acts 8:27, see 37.77. See also 93.209.

senses.def: to see, frequently in the sense of becoming aware of or taking notice of something
to have the faculty of sight

senses.subdomain: Be Ready To Learn, Pay Attention
senses.def: (figurative extension of meaning of βλέπω[a] ‘to see,’ 24.7) to be ready to learn about future dangers or needs, with the implication of preparedness to respond appropriately
to process information by giving consideration to various aspects
senses.comment: In a number of languages the concept of thinking is closely related to terms referring to perception. For example, in some languages one may speak of thinking as ‘to see with the heart’ or ‘to look at with the liver.’

senses.def: to come to understand as the result of perception
to take responsibility for causing something to happen
glosses: to see to it that something happens
to arrange for something to happen

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of βλέπω[a] ‘to see,’ 24.7) to be oriented in a particular direction

senses.subdomain: To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to see into the face) to judge on the basis of external appearances
glosses: to judge on the basis of appearance
to pay no attention to a person’s status
to judge on the basis of reputation
senses.comment: In some languages an equivalent of this expression in Matthew 22:16 may be ‘when you judge, you look into a man’s heart’ or ‘when you judge you see more than a person’s face’ or ‘when you judge a person, who he appears to be doesn’t count.’

senses.def: (derivative of Γαλατία ‘Galatia,’ 93.442) pertaining to Galatia

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: one who habitually fools or deceives people through pretense
pertaining to being religious
senses.comment: δεισιδαίμων may occur in either a good or a bad sense; that is to say, it may mean either ‘very religious’ or ‘superstitious,’ although the meaning of ‘superstitious’ is primarily a later development in the meaning of this word. In Acts 17:22 there seems every reason to believe that Paul was using the term in a positive sense.

senses.def: to tuck up or hold a garment firmly in place by wrapping a belt, girdle, or piece of cloth around it (compare ζώνη belt; girdle; 6.178)
glosses: to wear a narrow band of cloth around the waist

senses.def: any kind of food or nourishment
senses.comment: Almost all languages have at least a few general terms for food, though these may be derived from verbal expressions meaning essentially ‘that which is eaten.’ In some instances a distinction may be made between ‘that which is chewed’ and ‘that which is drunk,’ and it may therefore be important in certain contexts to speak of food in general by a phrase meaning ‘that which is either chewed or drunk.’ If one fails to include both types of food, the reader might interpret a passage such as Matthew 6:11 as requesting only solid foods.|In the place of a general term or phrase such as ‘that which is eaten’ or ‘that which is consumed,’ some languages generalize the meaning of a particular term. For example, in certain parts of the Orient the term meaning specifically ‘rice’ also refers to ‘food’ in general. In fact, some persons will declare, ‘I have not eaten!’ if they have not had rice as part of a meal. A similar type of meaning has developed in English with respect to ‘bread.’ For example, in rendering Luke 4:4 (οὐκ ἐπ’ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ‘man shall not live by bread alone’) it would be wrong to employ a strictly literal rendering, since this might mean simply that people should not live on a diet consisting solely of bread. The meaning of Luke 4:4 is, of course, ‘to live means more than merely eating.’

senses.def: to think that something may not be true or certain
senses.comment: In a number of languages ‘doubt’ is expressed by means of idioms, for example, ‘to have two thoughts’ or ‘to think only perhaps’ or ‘to believe only a little’ or ‘to question one’s heart about.’

senses.def: attributing ill repute or bad reputation to
a marker of a condition, real or hypothetical, actual or contrary to fact
a marker of cause or reason on the basis that an actual case is regarded formally as a supposition
senses.comment: In English it is possible to translate εἰ in passages such as Romans 6:8 and Matthew 6:30 as either ‘if’ or ‘since,’ for the conjunction ‘if’ may also refer to an actual event as a supposition. In a number of languages, however, it is impossible to translate ‘if God so clothes the grass of the field,’ for this would imply serious doubt as to whether God actually does perform such an activity. It may therefore be necessary in such languages to translate quite specifically ‘because’ or ‘since.’

senses.def: a marker of an indirect question as content
a marker of contrast by designating an exception
a marker of considerable emphasis (in comparison with δήπου[b], 91.7)
(an idiom, literally: if it should happen) a marker of a degree of probability
extension from a source which is away from the speaker
an untimely or premature birth
senses.comment: There is a certain fundamental problem involved in the rendering of ἔκτρωμα in 1 Corinthians 15:8. Here Paul refers to himself, but the event in question is the appearance of Jesus to Paul, evidently on the road to Damascus. The reference, therefore, would seem to be his being born as a Christian. This spiritual birth, however, would appear to be rather late in the process rather than premature. It is for this reason that it may be wise to translate ἔκτρωμα in some instances as ‘untimely birth’ or ‘born at the wrong time,’ rather than indicating that he was ‘born too soon.’

senses.def: to cause someone to go into, as in the case of a boat
senses.comment: The causative in this type of context may be expressed simply as ‘he commanded us,’ or the causative may be somewhat weakened to a form such as in English ‘he had us go aboard.’

senses.def: cardinal number, where there are ninety instances of a countable entity
to begin vegetative growth, with special emphasis upon the sprouting of leaves
senses.comment: The initial stages of growth, either of a plant as a whole or in the renewal of foliage after a winter or dry season, may be expressed in a number of ways, for example, ‘to become green again,’ ‘to show leaves,’ ‘to see leaves begin,’ or ‘when leaves unfold.’

senses.def: to continue to be in a state in or on someone, with the implication of beneficent result
(a figurative extension of meaning of ἐπαναπαύομαι ‘to remain upon something or someone,’ not occurring in the NT) to continue to believe firmly in someone or something and thus to rely upon
senses.comment: The concept of dependence or reliance upon something may be expressed in a number of different ways. For example, the phrase ἐπαναπαύω νόμῳ in Romans 2:17 may be rendered in some languages as ‘you believe that all you need is the Law’ or ‘you believe the Law will help you in every way.’

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἐπικαλύπτω ‘to cover over, to put a covering on,’ not occurring in the NT) to cause sin to be forgiven
to give detailed instructions as to what must be done
a person in the genealogy of Jesus
pertaining to being easily persuaded, with the implication of being open to reason or willing to listen

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Binding and Fastening
senses.def: an instrument for joining together objects (normally two)
senses.comment: In Acts 27:40 ζευκτηρία refers to ropes employed in linking two rudders of a boat. In most languages, however, one would simply use a term for ‘rope.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to a quiet, peaceful existence or attitude
the female of any living creature
King Ahabs notorious queen

senses.subdomain: Same or Equivalent Kind or Class
senses.def: pertaining to that which is of equal significance or value
to acquire definite information, and with focus upon the process of perception
to be a financial burden to someone by requiring too much support
glosses: to be a financial burden to

senses.def: to so influence others as to cause them to follow a recommended course of action
senses.comment: In some languages it is difficult to distinguish readily between expressions for ‘leading’ and those which refer to ‘ruling’ or ‘governing,’ but it is important to try to distinguish clearly between these two different sets of interpersonal relations. In some languages, the concept of ‘leading’ can be expressed by ‘showing how to’ or ‘demonstrating how one ought to.’ In other languages it is possible to speak of ‘leading’ as simply ‘going ahead of,’ but too often such an expression may designate only ‘a scout’ who goes ahead to see whether things are safe, or it may refer only to a person who insists on his prerogative as the most distinguished person in a group.

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to guide the feet properly) to guide or direct behavior in an appropriate manner
(a borrowing from Latin) a tax paid by each adult male to the government
senses.comment: See discussion at 57.179.

senses.def: to cause something to become unclean, profane, or ritually unacceptable
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is quite impossible to translate literally the concept of unclean, for physical cleanliness and ritual acceptability are completely unrelated. In some languages it is necessary to translate κοινόω[a] or βεβηλόω as to take away its holiness or to make something unacceptable to God. In many cultures one must express this concept as involving so-called negative taboo.

senses.def: to call or to regard something as common or defiled

senses.subdomain: High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
senses.def: pertaining to having noble status, with the implication of power and authority, often employed as a title

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: the dead body of a person, especially one which is still unburied
senses.comment: Though in Hebrews 3:17 the Greek text reads literally ‘whose dead bodies fell in the wilderness,’ it would normally be a mistake to translate this clause literally, since it might suggest that the people died while they were still standing, and that only the corpses fell. A more natural equivalent is ‘they died in the wilderness’ or ‘they died and their bodies lay in the wilderness.’

senses.def: speech which is complete and utter nonsense
talk which has no beneficial purpose and is thus idle and meaningless
(literally: one who has been anointed) in the NT, titles for Jesus as the Messiah, but in many contexts, and especially without an article, Χριστός becomes a part of the name of Jesus; see 93.387)
senses.comment: In a number of languages Χριστός (or Μεσσίας) as a reference to the Messiah occurs in a transliterated form based either on Χριστός in Greek or on Messiah in Hebrew. However, in some languages an attempt is made to represent the significance of the terms Χριστός and Μεσσίας by translating ‘God’s appointed one’ or ‘God’s specially chosen one’ or ‘the expected one,’ in the sense of one to whom everyone was looking for help and deliverance.

senses.def: (derivative of μίγνυμι ‘to mix, to mingle,’ 63.10) that which has been mixed
a strongly aromatic and expensive ointment
senses.comment: μύρον as a ‘perfume’ may be rendered as ‘sweet-smelling oil’ or ‘fragrant oil.’ In Luke 23:56 one may use a descriptive phrase such as ‘perfumed oil for preserving the body’ or ‘… to keep the body from rotting.’

senses.def: one of the seven helpers in the church in Jerusalem
a reference to an entity regarded as relatively present in terms of the discourse setting, whether preceding or following
a reference to indefinite alternatives
fruit of the fig tree συκῆ, produced late in the summer season (and often falling off before it ripens)
senses.comment: In the only context in which ὄλυνθος occurs in the NT (Revelation 6:13), one may employ an expression such as ‘unripe fig’ or ‘fig which ripens late.’

senses.def: to live a life of moral correctness
glosses: to live as one ought to
senses.comment: ὀρθοποδέω may be translated in a number of languages as ‘to live as one should.’

senses.def: (derivative of ὀφείλω[a] ‘to owe,’ 57.219) that which is owed
that which ought to be done as a matter of duty or social obligation
to speak in such a way as to encourage a particular type of behavior or action

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: experience of the winter season
pertaining to being level or flat, in contrast with what is steep or uneven
to live near and around
to believe something to be true and, hence, worthy of being trusted
senses.comment: In a number of languages the equivalent of πιστεύω[a] is simply to think to be true or to regard as true, but in some languages an idiomatic expression is employed, for example, to think in the heart or to think in the liver or to hold in the heart.

senses.def: to believe to the extent of complete trust and reliance
senses.comment: In rendering πιστεύω[b] and πίστις[b] it would be wrong to select a term which would mean merely ‘reliance’ or ‘dependency’ or even ‘confidence,’ for there should also be a significant measure of ‘belief,’ since real trust, confidence, and reliance can only be placed in someone who is believed to have the qualities attributed to such a person.

senses.def: to believe in the good news about Jesus Christ and to become a follower
to entrust something to the care of someone
glosses: to put into the care of
senses.comment: In some languages it may be possible to render this expression in Romans 3:2 as ‘because God gave his message to them to take care of’ or ‘… to keep,’ but one should avoid the implication that the message was simply to be kept by the Jews for themselves.

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ποίμνιον ‘flock,’ not occurring in the NT) the followers of Christ constituting a well-defined membership group
glosses: people who are like a flock
senses.comment: It is often impossible to reproduce the figurative values of ἀρνίον[b] (11.29), πρόβατον[b] (11.30), ποίμνιον, and ποίμνη[b],, since such metaphors cannot be employed in areas of the world in which sheep serve primarily as scavengers around villages (something which is generally true in many parts of the tropics). It may be possible in some instances to preserve something of the metaphorical value of these four terms by translating in some such manner as ‘take care of my people as you would sheep’ or ‘take care of my people, who are like sheep,’ or ‘take care of my helpless people,’ but frequently one can only translate as ‘take care of my people.’

senses.def: an officer of a court responsible for carrying out the orders of a judge
to cause to be in force in advance
senses.comment: In some languages an equivalent of this expression in Galatians 3:17 may be ‘God tied the covenant in advance.’

senses.def: to moor a ship in a safe place, either by anchor or possibly by drawing up on a beach

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Agriculture and Husbandry
senses.def: a fork-like shovel for throwing threshed grain into the air so that the wind may separate the chaff from the grain
senses.comment: Where there is no receptor-language term for a winnowing shovel, one may use a descriptive phrase, for example, ‘a tool for throwing threshed grain into the air in order to let the chaff blow away.’

senses.def: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

senses.subdomain: Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
senses.def: sapphire, usually blue in color (see 2.29)
a country at the western end of the Mediterranean Sea
a covered colonnade, open normally on one side, where people could stand, sit, or walk, protected from the weather and the heat of the sun
senses.comment: Also see comments at 7.58.|In many parts of the world the closest equivalent to a στοά would be a veranda, an extensive type of porch. Such a porch may be described as ‘a long outside room’ or ‘a room made with pillars and open.’

senses.def: a deciduous fruit tree growing to about 6 m; produces black berries containing a sweet reddish juice
senses.comment: For languages which have no specific term for ‘mulberry tree,’ one can often employ a generic expression followed by a type of classifier, for example, ‘the tree called mulberry’ (in which case the term ‘mulberry’ may be borrowed from a dominant language of the area) or ‘a tree producing berries’; but in Luke 17:6 the focus is upon the tree as a large object and not upon the type of fruit which it produced. One can, therefore, say simply ‘this tree.’

senses.def: to accompany someone, with explicit marking of association
to work out a joint arrangement
to function as a tetrarch (see 37.78)
glosses: to be the governor of a region

senses.def: to run, with emphasis upon relative speed in contrast with walking
senses.comment: τρέχω[a] also occurs in figurative contexts: δι᾽ ὑπομονῆς τρέχωμεν τὸν προκείμενον ἡμῖν ἀγῶνα ‘let us run with determination the race that is before us’ Hebrews 12:1.

senses.def: to try to do something (employed in the absolute construction)
to make progress in one’s behavior or conduct
senses.comment: It may also be possible to translate ἐτρέχετε καλῶς as ‘you were doing better and better.’

senses.def: a clear liquid that is without color, taste, or smell in its pure form; it forms rivers, lakes, and oceans, and sustains life on earth
senses.comment: In 2 Peter 3:5 the Greek expression is admittedly both strange and obscure. ἐξ ὕδατος presumably refers to the fact that the land emerged from the water, or at least was separated from the water. The phrase δἰ ὕδατος, literally ‘through water,’ may be locative, that is to say, it may refer to a place, but it is more likely to have some reference to water as an instrument which contributed to the act of producing the heavens and earth. However, the active instrument for this creation was τῷ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγῳ ‘the word of God.’. Since the dative case ὕδατι ‘by water’ is clearly instrumental in verse 6, it may be that ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ δἰ ὕδατος in verse 5 refers in a spacial sense to the formation of the heavens and the dry land ‘from water and through a watery area.’|Even more complex, however, than the interpretation of ‘water’ in 2 Peter 3:5 is the fact that in a number of languages there are quite different terms for ὕδωρ depending upon the type of water, its location, and its function. For example, water in some kind of bowl or container (and thus most likely used for drinking or cooking) may be referred to by one term, while water in a lake, stream, or ocean may be identified by quite a different term. Similarly, an important distinction may be made between salt water and fresh water, and an even further distinction may be introduced in the case of brackish water, that is to say, water which is partially salty. Some languages make a distinction between water which collects in pools and water which is flowing in streams or rivers. Accordingly, careful attention must be paid to contexts in order to select the appropriate term for ὕδωρ (see also 8.64 on John 19:34).

senses.def: a position below another position or object
a position on the undersurface of an object
to be under the complete control of someone
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is simply not possible to preserve the idiom ‘under the feet of,’ though in some instances one may use a parallel idiom, for example, ‘to stand on,’ so that 1 Corinthians 15:25 might be rendered ‘until he stands on all his enemies,’ but it is more likely that the idiom in this context is better rendered as ‘until he defeats all his enemies.’

senses.def: the use of magic, often involving drugs and the casting of spells upon people
senses.comment: φαρμακεία and the variant φάρμακον (as in Revelation 9:21) differ from the preceding terms (53.96-53.99) in that the focus is upon the use of certain potions or drugs and the casting of spells.

senses.def: pertaining to something or someone who causes fear
frozen rain
senses.comment: In Revelation 8:7 and Revelation 16:21 it is possible that χάλαζα is better interpreted as referring to a ‘hailstorm.’|In a number of languages hail is described as ‘frozen rain,’ but it may be referred to by more idiomatic expressions such as ‘cloud stones’ or ‘ice stones.’

senses.def: to conduct oneself in a particular manner with regard to some person
to behave or to conduct oneself with respect to certain means
to engage in the activity of making use of something
to make use of instruments
senses.comment: In Acts 27:17 βοηθεία is best regarded as a technical nautical term for supports (ropes or cables) used in aiding a ship in danger (see 35.10).

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ψύχομαι ‘to become cold,’ not occurring in the NT) to diminish significantly in intensity
